I checked all 11 issues against the code: 4 are valid, 3 partly valid, 2 are matters of style and 2 are wrong. I didn't change any code or post any replies. The verdicts are in `verdicts.json`, which parses as valid JSON.

**Summary:** 4 valid (3 need a code change, 1 optional) · 3 partly valid (optional) · 2 style preference · 2 invalid

| # | Issue | Verdict | Change code? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Deleting the cache doesn't refresh `connectedCalendars` | VALID | YES |
| 1 | Date format hardcoded to `"en-US"` | VALID | YES |
| 2 | Only credential owners can delete; team members can't | INVALID | NO |
| 3 | Script relies on `/tmp/tmole.log` when tmole is already running | PARTIALLY_VALID | OPTIONAL |
| 4 | `sed -i ''` fails on GNU sed (Linux) | VALID | YES |
| 5 | `npx tsx` instead of adding tsx as a devDependency | VALID | OPTIONAL |
| 6 | Unused loop variable `i` | STYLE_PREFERENCE | OPTIONAL |
| 7 | Mock method omits the parameter | STYLE_PREFERENCE | NO |
| 8 | No guard for missing or duplicate credential IDs | INVALID | NO |
| 9 | Use `z.number().int().positive()` | PARTIALLY_VALID | OPTIONAL |
| 10 | Return early on an empty list and remove duplicate IDs | PARTIALLY_VALID | OPTIONAL |

**Why the main ones landed where they did:**
- **#0:** The delete-cache mutation only calls `onSuccess?.()`, while the disconnect mutation refreshes the list itself (`CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:42-64`). `EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372` shows the dropdown without passing `onChanged`, and the cache options still appear there. After a delete on that page, the "last updated" time stays stale.
- **#4:** On Linux, GNU sed treats `''` as the edit command and the real `s|...|` expression as a file name, so it errors. The script still prints "✅ Updated", but `.env` is never changed (`scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:69`).
- **#1:** The rest of the codebase formats dates with the user's language (`i18n.language`), e.g. `ViewRecordingsDialog.tsx:174`.
- **#2:** This dropdown only lists the user's own credentials (`getUsersCredentials.ts:13-22` filters on `userId`) plus delegation credentials. Team credentials never reach this screen, so the owner-only check blocks nothing.
- **#7 / #8:** TypeScript accepts a method with fewer parameters, and the other mocks in that file already leave them out. Every credential ID is typed as a required number, and repeated IDs don't affect the results of an `in` query.
- **#9 / #10:** These are safe as written. The owner check rejects bad IDs, and Prisma returns an empty result for an empty list. The suggestions are minor hardening or save one database round-trip.
